Q: Thank you for agreeing to give this recorded statement. Please state your full name for the record.
A: I'd rather not give my name on the recording, but you have my claim file, so you can use that.
Q: That's fine. Can you tell me where you were when the collision happened?
A: I was in Katy, Texas, turning left at a major intersection. I was heading into a shopping center parking lot.
Q: Did you have a green light or a turn arrow?
A: It was a green ball, and I was waiting for a gap in oncoming traffic. There was a car coming at me that I thought
was far enough away.
Q: What happened next?
A: I started the turn and then the other vehicle hit the front driver's side of my car. It came in fast, and I didn't see it
until it was almost on me.
Q: Were you wearing your seatbelt?
A: Yes, and the airbags deployed. My head hit the side window and the steering wheel.
Q: How are you feeling now?
A: Not good. I have headaches, I'm sensitive to light, and I get dizzy when I stand up too fast. My doctor said I have a
concussion and I need to limit screen time and rest.
Q: Have you been seen by any medical providers since the accident?
A: Yes, I went to the emergency room the same day and I'm following up with my primary care doctor and a
neurologist. I have records from all of them.
Q: Did anyone else in the vehicle get hurt?
A: No, I was alone in the car.
Q: Is there anything else you want to add to your statement?
A: Only that I've been unable to work since the collision, and I'm worried about how long recovery will take.
Q: Thank you. That concludes the statement.
A: Thank you.
</page>

injury. Do not list the date of a note, letter, report, visit, statement, filing or signature.

it is the loss date. Examples: "Date of loss:", "Crash date:", "Date of injury:", "the collision on".
